desc:
A network has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1. Each entry edges[i] = [a, b] is a two-way connection between nodes a and b. No pair of nodes is joined by more than one edge and no node is joined to itself.

Return true if you can travel from node source to node destination by following connections, and false otherwise. A node can always reach itself.
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b, source, destination < n, and a ≠ b
No two edges join the same pair of nodes
hints: Think of the connections as a graph. The question is whether two nodes lie in the same connected piece.
Starting from source, repeatedly visit neighbours you have not seen yet (BFS or DFS) and note everything you reach.
Build an adjacency list first, keep a visited array, and stop early when you pop destination. Use an explicit queue or stack so a 2,000-node chain cannot overflow the recursion limit.
editorial: Turn the edge list into an adjacency list, adding each edge in both directions. Run a breadth-first search from source, marking nodes as visited when they are first put on the queue. If destination is ever reached the answer is true; if the queue empties first, it is false. When source and destination are the same node the search succeeds immediately.

A union-find structure is an equally good alternative: union the endpoints of every edge, then compare the representatives of the two nodes. It never builds an adjacency list and is handy if the question has to be answered for many pairs. Both approaches take O(n + m) time.
